title: Soft Denier + Staged Escrow Degrader for Model Dependencies
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a new multi-layer protection mechanism for model/dependency/tenant failures that trips in controlled stages and provides audited, reversible degradations. This ticket builds 'Soft Denier' (a probabilistic request gate) and 'Staged Escrow' (a transient degraded mode that serves cached/cheaper variants and short-lived synthetic responses) to avoid wholesale outages during spikes, region outages, or model regressions. The design must be per-entity (model, dependency, tenant) and integrate with existing routing/fallback plumbing and rollout tooling.
success_criteria: 1) Breaker state machine deployed to staging and affects <=10% traffic during canary. 2) For injected latency/error scenarios, system transitions to SOFT_DEGRADE/ESCROW instead of OPEN with >90% availability for non-blocked tenants. 3) SLO breach rate for critical tenants reduced by 50% vs current behavior during faults. 4) Observability dashboards and runbook pages published and approved.
design_notes:
Core ideas:
- Per-entity state machine: CLOSED -> SOFT_DEGRADE -> ESCROW_OPEN -> PROBATION -> CLOSED. Soft Degrade is probabilistic rejection/priority reduction. Escrow Open is deterministic degraded path with strict time-to-live (default 30s) and eviction counters.
- Trip logic is hybrid: (a) sustained P95 latency above threshold AND rapidly rising error rate OR (b) error budget consumption > 80% within a rolling window => move to SOFT_DEGRADE. If condition persists for N consecutive windows, escalate to ESCROW_OPEN.
- Use dual-window counters: short window (30s) for spike detection, long window (5m) for stability assessment. Hysteresis applied by requiring K windows to pass for state changes.
- Soft Denier implementation: a token-bucket inspired probabilistic gate that denies based on current load + entity weight; responses are 429/Retry-After for non-critical callers and internal queueing / background retry for high-priority routes.
- Escrow behaviors: route to (in order) prefix cache, cached model responses, cheaper/quantized model variant, or a small deterministic fallback transformer that returns structured partial results. Explicitly avoid returning stale or inconsistent outputs for sensitive tenants—use tenant allowlists for read-only synthetic responses.
- Safe fallback rules stored in configuration with per-tenant overrides and per-model affinity scoring. All transitions are logged with a causal_id for audit.
trip_thresholds:
Default thresholds (tunable per-entity):
- Latency path: P95 > 1,200ms (short window 30s) AND 95th_torque_ratio_increase > 1.5x -> SOFT_DEGRADE. If persists for 3 short windows -> ESCROW_OPEN.
- Error path: 5% error rate over 30s and error_budget_consumption >= 80% over 5m -> SOFT_DEGRADE. Persist for 2 long windows -> ESCROW_OPEN.
- Backoff: PROBATION period is 60s then allow a small fraction (10%) of traffic to test recovery. Full close requires 5m of healthy windows.
- Tenant weight and SLA can raise or lower thresholds: enterprise tenants default 2x multiplier on thresholds (more tolerant) unless 'protective' flag set.
telemetry_and_alerting:
Metrics to emit:
- breaker.state{entity_type,entity_id}: CLOSED|SOFT_DEGRADE|ESCROW_OPEN|PROBATION
- breaker.trip_reason{entity_type,entity_id}: latency|error|resource
- breaker.trip_count{entity_type,entity_id}
- breaker.denied_count, breaker.degraded_count, fallback.rate
- model.p95_latency_ms, model.error_rate, model.cpu_util_pct, model.gpu_mem_pct
Dashboards: per-region per-model breaker overview, exploded tenant impact, and a global 'Escrow Pool' view. Alerts:
- Pager if ESCROW_OPEN triggered for >5% of total requests across production for >2min
- Pager if a single tenant enters ESCROW_OPEN and has 'high' customer_impact
- SLO alert if degradation increases error_budget consumption by >10% relative to baseline.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + infra): feature flags, config schema, metric names (2 weeks). Phase 2 (soft denier): implement probabilistic gate in front of routing layer + unit tests (1 sprint). Phase 3 (staged escrow): implement routing to cache/quantized variants + synthetic response generator + audit logs (2 sprints). Phase 4 (integration tests & observability): chaos tests, dashboards, runbook (1 sprint). Phase 5 (canary rollout): 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback gates. Code lives in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/escrow-gates. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1209 and /pull/1218.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for state transitions with mocked metrics.
- Integration in staging: inject latency/error into model-serving path and verify transitions (use k6 + chaos monkey). Test matrix covers: single-tenant spike, cross-tenant spike, regional outage, model regression (higher error rate).
- Performance: ensure added gate adds <1ms median overhead at p95 additional <5ms under 95th percentile traffic.
- Safety: automated rollback if customer-impacting tenants experience >5% increase in 5m error budget burn.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag OFF by default. 2) Canary to non-production traffic and internal tenants. 3) Enable for 10% prod traffic with analytics only (no enforce). 4) Enable enforcement for 10% then increment to 50% after 24h if no pager events. 5) Widen to 100% with staged tenant opt-outs for sensitive customers.
runbook_and_ops: Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ESCROW-SoftDenier (draft). Runbook contains steps to: force-close a breaker, drain an escrow pool, extract audit trail for a given causal_id, and emergency rollback steps for feature flags. On-call playbook: acknowledge pager -> identify entity_id -> check 'breaker.state' panel -> if ESCROW_OPEN and false-positive, force PROBATION for 60s and open incident.
dependencies_notes: Needs model-variant routing hooks from ENG-662241. Requires observability dimension work (tagging by tenant) from ENG-712900. KMS key access for audit logs is handled by SEC-1201 (coordination required).
